problemStatement.formal: In Euclidean geometry, prove that dist A B = dist A C implies angle A B C = angle A C B.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize Euclid I.5, the isosceles triangle theorem: equal sides in a triangle imply equal base angles.
whyMatters: Euclid I.5 is one of the classical first tests of a geometry formalization.
The proof connects a synthetic congruence argument with Lean's inner-product-space angle API.
The companion theorem exposes both the direct Mathlib route and a Pappus-style self-congruence proof.

proven: The direct companion file proves base-angle equality from equal side lengths (Lean: base_angles_equal_of_sides_equal).
The OQ file proves Pappus's self-congruence version of Euclid I.5 using equal-norm vector angle symmetry (Lean: pappus_isosceles).
A documented auxiliary lemma captures Euclid's outer-segment equality step for extended equal sides (Lean: euclid_outer_segs_eq).
The final Euclid-named theorem restates the base-angle conclusion as Pons Asinorum (Lean: euclid_i5).
knownResults.goal: Document the verified Euclid I.5 formalization and its Pappus-style Lean proof route.

currentState.focus: Pappus proof formalized. Gallery entry created.
